article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Morning Brief
article.dek: Overnight the market moved — Chicago's moneyline drifted to -184, the plus-EV Dolphins read from last night is off the board, and Breece Hall is out for Sunday.

items.headline: The Value lane is empty this morning
paragraphs: The overnight market moved, and the board followed. The Dolphins +10.5 at -110 that the model priced plus-EV last night now costs -120 at FanDuel for the same 10.5 points, and the edge is gone. No other offer clears the Value lane's frozen contract, so the lane reads NO_PLAY.

Chicago's moneyline drifted too — from -176 to -184 at FanDuel (DraftKings -185, Pinnacle -192) — and the Balanced lane rotated off the Bears' spread onto the Eagles getting 3.5 points at home against the Rams. If you grabbed the Dolphins number last night, it's in your pocket. Don't chase a new one this morning.
items.takeaway: Overnight juice killed last night's plus-EV read; the Value lane is empty and the board's two plays both cost more than yesterday.

items.headline: The injury news, all in one place
paragraphs: The biggest new development: the Jets ruled out running back Breece Hall (quad) for Sunday at Chicago — the Jets lose their lead back. Also out for the Jets: Kiko Mauigoa, AD Mitchell, Dylan Parham and Mason Taylor, with Kenyon Sadiq and Kingsley Enagbare questionable. On the Bears' side, Caleb Williams and Braxton Jones stay out (Case Keenum starts), joined by Kyler Gordon, Noah Swell and Shemar Turner; Cam Lewis is doubtful. D'Andre Swift will play.

Elsewhere: Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (right shoulder) will play, and Morgan Moses is questionable after returning to practice; Gonzalez, Barmore and Schooler are out. For Buffalo, Keon Coleman is expected to play while Christian Benford (DNP Friday) is questionable. Denver is thin at edge rusher with Dondrea Tillman out and Jonathon Cooper on the exempt list; Mims, Waddle and Dobbins are cleared. The 49ers' Nick Bosa has conflicting late-week reports — one lists him questionable, another says the Niners expect to be without him, so watch the inactive list. Houston loses Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin); Nico Collins practiced fully Friday. Green Bay's Edgerrin Cooper (concussion) was a full Friday participant and is trending toward playing, while rookie Jager Burton is newly questionable. Justin Jefferson stays out for Minnesota; Baker Mayfield is out several weeks in Tampa, where Jalon Daniels starts. The app's expected starters match all of Friday's reporting — no new quarterback changes overnight.
items.takeaway: Hall out is the headline; Bosa's status is genuinely uncertain; everything else is Friday's designations standing.

items.headline: Sunday weather: the final look
paragraphs: Two games carry a real chance of rain at kickoff: Philadelphia (Rams at Eagles, 1 p.m. ET — 56%) and Baltimore (Titans at Ravens, 1 p.m. ET — 55%), both in the mid-60s. MetLife (Cardinals at Giants) and Charlotte for Sunday night (Lions at Panthers) each sit at a chance of showers.

The heat games: Tampa hits 88 with scattered storms possible after 2 p.m., and Santa Clara carries a National Weather Service heat warning — 92 to 94 at kickoff for Broncos at 49ers, one of the hottest games in Broncos history. Houston's roof game is unaffected with storms outside. London (Colts at Commanders, 9:30 a.m. ET) is 67 and partly cloudy; Buffalo, Chicago, Cincinnati and Seattle are all calm and clear. The two domes are weather-proof.
items.takeaway: Rain is likely in Philadelphia and Baltimore; Tampa and Santa Clara are the heat games; everything else is manageable.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Hit Rate: still Chicago, at a thinner price
paragraphs: The Hit Rate card answers one question: which supported pick looks most likely to win. This morning it still says Chicago's moneyline — model 70.07%, trust 66.89%. The price moved against us overnight (-176 to -184 at FanDuel), and the EV sits at -1.78%.

That negative number is not a flaw in the card. The app's own tutorial says Hit Rate ≠ Profit Rate: this lane forgoes value for win probability on purpose. The market drifting Chicago's way is information — the board agrees with the model more than it did yesterday — not an instruction to bet bigger. The app sizes the stake from your bankroll, deliberately conservative.
items.takeaway: Chicago is the most-likely-to-win supported read; the thinner price doesn't change the card's job.

items.headline: Balanced: the middle lane moved to Philadelphia
paragraphs: Balanced is the middle ground — a strong pick without paying too much, and a good starting point for a new bettor. This morning it reads the Eagles +3.5 at -105 at FanDuel (model 50.52%, play-through -108): Philadelphia getting points at home in likely rain against the Rams.
The lane rotated off the Bears' spread overnight as the numbers shifted. The card follows the price — when the market reprices the slate, the middle-ground read moves with it.
items.takeaway: The middle lane is Eagles +3.5 at home; the card follows the price.

items.headline: Value: empty is a read
paragraphs: Value is always the model's plus-EV play — the price-beats-market read. This morning no offer clears the frozen contract, so the lane is empty. The market is simply priced too tight for the model's edge bar.
An empty lane is the model saying 'not today.' The disciplined move is patience, not pressing the other two cards harder to fill the gap.
items.takeaway: No plus-EV offer this morning — patience is the read, not forcing a bet.

items.headline: Overnight: the market moved, the board followed
paragraphs: Chicago's moneyline went from -176 to -184 at FanDuel overnight (DraftKings -185, Pinnacle -192), with the app's play-through at -189 — the price got worse for bettors and the card's EV slid from -0.22% to -1.78%. The Dolphins' 10.5 points went from -110 to -120 at FanDuel for the identical line, and that juice is what killed last night's plus-EV Value read; DraftKings moved the Dolphins to 10.0 outright.

The Balanced lane's recommendation was replaced: Chicago -3.5 at -104 is out, Philadelphia +3.5 at -105 is in (play-through -108). The 6:00 board has all of it. But the board's prices are FanDuel and DraftKings — your book's number is what you're actually betting. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: The moves are in the board — bet your book's number, not the board's; Check prices your actual ticket.

items.headline: Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff
paragraphs: The morning brief can't have the inactive lists — they drop about 90 minutes before each kickoff, and the first one comes early with the London game at 9:30 a.m. ET. The questionable tags worth watching: Bosa (conflicting reports), Cooper (concussion, trending the right way), Benford (DNP Friday), Moses (foot), and Sadiq and Enagbare for the Jets.
The board refreshes every morning and evening. If a designation flips after the board, don't guess — type your book's line into Check and let the app re-price the ticket at your number.
items.takeaway: Watch the 90-minute lists, starting early for London; Check re-prices anything that flips.

items.headline: Betting term of the day: juice
paragraphs: Juice is the book's fee baked into the price — the -120 in Dolphins +10.5 -120. Last night the same 10.5 points cost -110; this morning they cost -120. Same points, higher fee. That juice movement is exactly what killed the Value lane's plus-EV read overnight.

Odds are just price mechanics: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. When the points stay put and the price climbs, you're paying more for the same ticket — and the app's math notices before your eyes do.
items.takeaway: Same points, higher fee — juice movement is what emptied the Value lane.

QB projections: Case Keenum (CHI), Jameis Winston (NYG), Marcus Mariota (WAS), Cam Ward starter (TEN), Jalon Daniels (TB), Kirk Cousins (LV), Jacoby Brissett (ARI), Kyler Murray (MIN), Malik Willis (MIA) — all match Friday's reporting; no new QB changes overnight.

evidence.app_guidance: Use the real board numbers; if your book's price differs from the board's FanDuel/DraftKings price, use Check to re-price the pick at your number.

evidence.fact: Attempted VSiN betting-splits check for a verified public-vs-sharper split on Week 4 NFL games, Saturday ~6:20am Denver. The free featured-game row on data.vsin.com/betting-splits is still Friday's college game (Pittsburgh +1.5 vs Virginia Tech -1.5): spread splits show Virginia Tech with 63% of handle and 70% of tickets — handle and tickets agree on the same side, which is NOT a disagreement. No free NFL tickets/handle row is visible; the full board is VSiN Pro paid. No Fade qualifies on NFL games this morning.
evidence.interpretation: Agreement between tickets and handle is popularity, not a signal. Without a verified disagreement plus corroborating movement, there is no Fade — the jargon item runs in today's tip instead.
evidence.app_guidance: The Fade is a decision layer, not a command to fade the public or override the app's cards.
